title: The kinain's spark
summary: What faerie blood gives the kinain.

claims.text: Kinain are only dimly aware of the Dreaming and have no fae mien or contact with chimera unless enchanted.

Their faerie heritage gives them a small spark of Glamour, never more than their faerie blood allows, and they have few ways to gain more, being too far from the true Dreaming; many trade on artistry, letting changelings share the Glamour their work creates.

A token can enchant whoever accepts it, even someone other than the intended recipient; mortals who know fae ways, such as some Autumn People and superstitious country folk, refuse any gift from a possible faerie, and the old warning against faerie food and gifts rests on fact.

title: Changelings and mages
summary: Why the Kithain keep away from mages.

claims.text: Tradition mages fight Banality in their own way, but most Kithain avoid mages, finding them power-hungry and their feuds too tangled to join.
The Technocracy is Banality made flesh to most fae, who avoid technomancers at all costs; the Technocracy wants to learn about the fae, perhaps by letting the Progenitors dissect a few.
Mages can be enchanted like mortals, though their magick lets them try to resist.
